riset-keyword-bisnis-lokal.title: How to Research Keywords for a Local Business Without Paid Tools
riset-keyword-bisnis-lokal.excerpt: The phrases nearby customers search for can be found in Google itself, no SEO tool subscription needed.
riset-keyword-bisnis-lokal.metaTitle: How to Research Keywords for a Local Business Without Paid Tools - OPTIMARK Blog
riset-keyword-bisnis-lokal.metaDescription: The phrases nearby customers search for can be found in Google itself, no SEO tool subscription needed.

blocks.text: A local business rarely needs thousands of keywords. It needs a handful of phrases real customers in your city type, and most of them can be found for free.
Start from the Google search box
Type your service plus your city name, then note the autocomplete suggestions and the “Related searches” at the bottom of the page. Both come from real searches.

items: Note autocomplete suggestions for service + city
Read the questions in the “People also ask” box
Check the wording competitors use in their Google Business Profile
Group phrases by intent: learn, compare, or buy

jadwal-posting-instagram-umkm-kuliner.title: The Best Instagram Posting Schedule for Food Businesses in 2026
jadwal-posting-instagram-umkm-kuliner.excerpt: There is no universal best time to post. For food businesses, your customers’ hungry hours are the benchmark.
jadwal-posting-instagram-umkm-kuliner.metaTitle: The Best Instagram Posting Schedule for Food Businesses in 2026 - OPTIMARK Blog
jadwal-posting-instagram-umkm-kuliner.metaDescription: There is no universal best time to post. For food businesses, your customers’ hungry hours are the benchmark.

blocks.text: “Best time to post on Instagram” articles usually give one number for every business. For food, a more honest benchmark is when your customers start thinking about their next meal.
Follow meal times, not office hours
Posting 30–60 minutes before lunch and dinner gives people time to see the post, then order. Check your account Insights to confirm the pattern.

items: Test the 10:30–11:30 and 16:30–17:30 slots for two weeks
Compare reach per slot in Instagram Insights
Save new-menu Reels for the weekend
Post promotions the day before payday

foto-produk-ai-smartphone.title: A Guide to Attractive Product Photos Using AI and a Smartphone
foto-produk-ai-smartphone.excerpt: Smartphone photos plus a little AI help are enough for a clean catalogue, as long as the source shot is right.
foto-produk-ai-smartphone.metaTitle: A Guide to Attractive Product Photos Using AI and a Smartphone - OPTIMARK Blog
foto-produk-ai-smartphone.metaDescription: Smartphone photos plus a little AI help are enough for a clean catalogue, as long as the source shot is right.

blocks.text: AI can clean up backgrounds, fix lighting, and create mood variations. But the result is only as good as the source photo you take on your phone.
Take a clean source photo
Use side light from a window, a plain background, and a camera level with the product. A sharp, bright photo gives the AI enough to work with.

items: Shoot near a window and avoid warm indoor bulbs
Wipe the lens before shooting
Take several angles of each product
Use AI for backgrounds and variations, not to change the product itself

strategi-content-pillar.title: A Content Pillar Strategy That Keeps Small Brands Posting Consistently
strategi-content-pillar.excerpt: Three or four content pillars mean you no longer wonder what to post every morning.
strategi-content-pillar.metaTitle: A Content Pillar Strategy That Keeps Small Brands Posting Consistently - OPTIMARK Blog
strategi-content-pillar.metaDescription: Three or four content pillars mean you no longer wonder what to post every morning.

blocks.text: Small brands rarely run out of ideas out of laziness. Usually every day starts from zero. Content pillars give you a frame so ideas don’t have to be found again.
Pick pillars from customer questions
Write down the questions customers ask most, then group them. Each group can become a pillar, for example education, product, behind the scenes, and testimonials.

items: Keep it to three or four pillars
Set a weekly share for each pillar
Keep five backup ideas per pillar
Review which pillar gets saved and shared most each month

website-belum-muncul-di-google.title: Why Your Website Isn’t on Google’s First Page Yet
website-belum-muncul-di-google.excerpt: Before blaming the algorithm, check whether Google can actually find and understand your pages.
website-belum-muncul-di-google.metaTitle: Why Your Website Isn’t on Google’s First Page Yet - OPTIMARK Blog
website-belum-muncul-di-google.metaDescription: Before blaming the algorithm, check whether Google can actually find and understand your pages.

blocks.text: A site missing from the first page doesn’t necessarily have bad content. Often Google hasn’t indexed the page, or can’t tell which search it answers.
Check indexing before content
Search site:yourdomain.com on Google. If important pages don’t show up, the problem is indexing, not writing. Google Search Console can show you why.

items: Register the site and sitemap in Google Search Console
Give every page a clear title and H1
Fix pages that load slowly on mobile
Link new pages from older pages that already get traffic

warna-feed-instagram.title: Tips for Choosing Instagram Feed Colours That Match Your Brand
warna-feed-instagram.excerpt: A consistent feed palette makes an account recognisable before anyone reads your brand name.
warna-feed-instagram.metaTitle: Tips for Choosing Instagram Feed Colours That Match Your Brand - OPTIMARK Blog
warna-feed-instagram.metaDescription: A consistent feed palette makes an account recognisable before anyone reads your brand name.

blocks.text: A tidy feed doesn’t mean every photo looks the same. What matters is two or three colours that keep appearing, so the account feels like one character.
Derive colours from your logo and product
Take one main colour from the logo, one neutral, and one accent from the product. Use all three in photo backgrounds, text, and props.

items: Keep the palette to three colours
Save the colour codes so designers and photographers agree
Use the same editing preset on every photo
Check the last nine posts in the grid before uploading

caption-tiktok.title: How to Write TikTok Captions That Get Viewers Interacting
caption-tiktok.excerpt: A good TikTok caption doesn’t repeat the video. It gives viewers a reason to comment.
caption-tiktok.metaTitle: How to Write TikTok Captions That Get Viewers Interacting - OPTIMARK Blog
caption-tiktok.metaDescription: A good TikTok caption doesn’t repeat the video. It gives viewers a reason to comment.

blocks.text: TikTok viewers have already watched the video. A caption that repeats it adds nothing. A good caption starts a conversation.
End with an easy question
Either-or questions like “Team spicy or team sweet?” are easier to answer than open ones. The lighter the answer, the more people comment.

items: Put the most important line first
Ask one either-or question at the end
Use three to five relevant hashtags
Reply to early comments within the first hour

artikel-jadi-konten-media-sosial.title: How to Turn One Blog Post Into Ten Social Media Posts
artikel-jadi-konten-media-sosial.excerpt: One well-researched article can feed two weeks of content without writing from scratch again.
artikel-jadi-konten-media-sosial.metaTitle: How to Turn One Blog Post Into Ten Social Media Posts - OPTIMARK Blog
artikel-jadi-konten-media-sosial.metaDescription: One well-researched article can feed two weeks of content without writing from scratch again.

blocks.text: A good blog post holds research, examples, and a conclusion. All of it can be broken into shorter social posts.
Split by point, not by paragraph
Each main point can become a carousel, each strong quote a text post, and each practical step a short video.

items: One carousel summarising the article
Three quote posts from the strongest lines
Three short videos, one per practical step
One poll and two stories to invite discussion

video-promosi-singkat.title: Making Short, Engaging Promo Videos Without Hiring an Editor
video-promosi-singkat.excerpt: A 15-second promo can be shot and edited on a smartphone, as long as the first three seconds are strong.
video-promosi-singkat.metaTitle: Making Short, Engaging Promo Videos Without Hiring an Editor - OPTIMARK Blog
video-promosi-singkat.metaDescription: A 15-second promo can be shot and edited on a smartphone, as long as the first three seconds are strong.

blocks.text: Viewers decide whether to keep watching or swipe within the first few seconds. Even a professional editor can’t save a video with a weak opening.
Open with the result, not the logo
Show the product in use or the end result in the first second. The logo and brand name can come at the end.

items: Plan three scenes: result, process, call to action
Shoot vertically in 9:16
Add on-screen text for people watching muted
Keep it to 15–30 seconds

target-audiens.title: Defining Your Target Audience Before Creating Content for an Online Business
target-audiens.excerpt: Content for everyone usually appeals to no one. Decide who you are talking to first.
target-audiens.metaTitle: Defining Your Target Audience Before Creating Content for an Online Business - OPTIMARK Blog
target-audiens.metaDescription: Content for everyone usually appeals to no one. Decide who you are talking to first.

blocks.text: Many online businesses start making content before they know who it is for. The result is polite content that doesn’t feel meant for anyone.
Start with customers who already bought
Look at your last ten customers: age, job, city, and why they bought. The pattern that shows up is where your target audience starts.

items: Interview three customers about why they bought
Write a one-paragraph ideal customer profile
Note the words they use when asking questions
Test content on one segment before widening

insight-instagram.title: Reading Instagram Insights to Find Your Most Effective Content
insight-instagram.excerpt: Likes aren’t the only measure. Saves and shares often show more honestly which content is useful.
insight-instagram.metaTitle: Reading Instagram Insights to Find Your Most Effective Content - OPTIMARK Blog
insight-instagram.metaDescription: Likes aren’t the only measure. Saves and shares often show more honestly which content is useful.

blocks.text: Instagram Insights offers plenty of numbers, and it’s easy to get lost. A few metrics are enough to decide which content to repeat.
Focus on saves and shares
Saved content is seen as useful, shared content as worth recommending. These two reflect a post’s value better than likes.

items: Compare posts by format: photo, carousel, Reels
Sort posts by number of saves
Note the posting times of your top five posts
Repeat the best topics in a different format
